proposals.hypothesis: LiAlO2 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating oxide with fully oxidized Al3+ that is hard to reduce, so it should resist reduction by LLZO and oxidation at 4.0 V vs Li. Its Al-O framework has no La or Zr, so it may avoid the LaNbO4, LaPO4, LaF3 and ZrO2 contact products that caused the earlier failures. LiAlO2 is also a known coating chemistry for LiCoO2 and garnet interfaces. This is an untested Al-based oxide family.

proposals.hypothesis: Li3TaO4 is a wide-gap, Li-rich tantalate with fully oxidized Ta5+ that resists reduction by LLZO and oxidation at 4.0 V. Its Ta-O framework lacks Zr and La, so it may avoid the La/Zr contact products that drove the earlier failures. Ta is the heavier congener of Nb, and the LiNbO3 coating gave the lowest penalty so far (0.082).
proposals.motivation: LiNbO3 (0.082) was the best contact penalty, and LiAlO2 (0.104) and Li3PO4 (0.099) failed mainly from La/Zr-bearing products. A Li-rich Ta5+ oxide keeps the group-5 Li-M-O chemistry that performed best while being a new chemical composition.

proposal.hypothesis: LiNbO3 is a wide-gap (~3.5 eV), electronically insulating Li-ion conductor that is a well-established buffer between LiCoO2 and sulfide or garnet electrolytes. Its Nb5+ is hard to reduce, so it should limit Co-O/LLZO interdiffusion and interfacial space-charge formation at 4.0 V, with a relatively low expected penalty.

Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, insulating lithium-ion conductor with fully oxidized P5+ that resists reduction by LLZO and oxidation at 4.0 V vs Li. Its Li-rich composition should give little chemical driving force for interdiffusion or new interphase products with either LiCoO2 or LLZO, so it may reach a lower contact penalty than LiNbO3.
proposal.motivation: The LiNbO3 coating (mp-aaacjjgb) had penalty 0.082 eV/atom in bin 4 and failed the 0.05 threshold, mainly from LaNbO4/ZrO2 formation at the LLZO contact. A Li-rich phosphate avoids the Nb-La-Zr reaction pathway.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2ZrO3 is a wide-gap, Li-rich zirconate. Because it already contains Zr4+, it should be closer to equilibrium with LLZO than LiNbO3 or Li3PO4, which both formed LaNbO4/LaPO4 and ZrO2 at the LLZO contact. Its Li2O-rich composition may also limit Co interdiffusion with LiCoO2 at 4.0 V.
proposal.motivation: Both prior coatings (LiNbO3 at 0.082 and Li3PO4 at 0.099 eV/atom, bin 4) failed mainly because of La/Zr-bearing reaction products at the LLZO contact. A coating that shares Zr with LLZO should reduce that driving force.

proposal.hypothesis: LiF is a very wide-gap, fully ionic Li-rich fluoride with no reducible or oxidizable transition-metal or oxyanion sites, so it should resist oxidation at 4.0 V vs Li and have little driving force to react with LLZO. Its contact products with LLZO would need to be fluorides of La or Zr, which are typically less favorable than the oxide-based products seen for LiNbO3, Li3PO4 and Li2ZrO3. It also offers a chemically different family from the oxide and phosphate coatings already tested.
proposal.motivation: Earlier LiNbO3 (0.082), Li3PO4 (0.099) and Li2ZrO3 (0.30 self-decomposition, 14 bin) all failed, and the first two were limited by La/Zr-oxide contact products. A halide with no oxide anion may avoid those pathways.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2O is a wide-gap, fully ionic, cation-free oxide with no reducible or oxidizable metal center. It is Li-rich and strongly basic, so it should have minimal driving force to form La- or Zr-bearing products with LLZO and should resist oxidation at 4.0 V vs Li. This is a chemically distinct, metal-free oxide from the earlier Nb, P, Zr and F coatings.

Li2ZrO3 failed self-decomposition. A coating with no transition or polyvalent cation may avoid these pathways.
